newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Investors recommended to sell Pakistan Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Investors recommended to sell Pakistan Telecom.

text.p: Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd was overvalued at its current price and investors were advised to sell the stock in a report issued by Credit Lyonnais Securities Asia.
Tuesday's report said Pakistan Telecom's earnings growth would average five percent a year over the next 10 years, down from an earlier forecast of 15 to 17 percent growth.

The brokerage forecast net revenue for 1996/97 (July-June) of 44.2 billion rupees ($1.09 billion), down from 49 billion rupees predicted earlier, while earnings per share were likely to grow 11 percent rather than above 20 percent.
Pakistan Telecom shares, majority-owned by the government, fell one rupee to 26.80 at Tuesday's close and dealers said the Credit Lyonnais report could lead to further falls.
The report said that, based on its earnings expectations, the present net value of Pakistan Telecom shares should be 19 rupees each, or 20 rupees if a tariff increase was factored in.
On the downside, it said Pakistan Telecom had agreed to a cut in rates with U.S.-based carriers in two tranches -- nine percent from January 1, 1997, and a further 10 percent from January 1, 1998.

Credit Lyonnais said volume growth of Pakistan Telecom's nationwide calls, which fell eight percent in the first six months of 1995/96, would remain modest because the government had taken away some major customers and handed them to the new state-run National Telecommunication Corp Ltd.
The former state-run Pakistan Telecommunications Corp was split into Pakistan Telecom and National Telecom in January 1996 as part of a government plan to privatise telecommunications.
Pakistan Telecom retained private sector telecommunications services while National Telecom took over services provided to the government.
Credit Lyonnais said it had first believed that National Telecom had been formed for security reasons and would only handle services for sensitive government departments such as defence.

But the transfer to National Telecom of other state-owned commercial organisations such as the Water and Power Development Authority, Karachi Electric Supply Corporation and Pakistan State Oil, would hurt revenue growth at Pakistan Telecom, it said.

The report said the transfer of high-volume customers to National Telecom and flat rental payments to it for use of its microwave network for the next three years would cause Pakistan Telecom a combined revenue loss of about three billion rupees ($74.59 million).

PTCL said last month net profit for 1995/96 fell to 14.269 billion rupees from 16.835 billion the previous year. Operating profit dropped to 16.554 billion rupees from 17.667 billion. Total revenue rose to 37.779 billion rupees from 33.060 billion.
